k1p1-4.name: text#4
k1p1-4.text: After KP06 the output layer gives a prediction; this unit asks how wrong it is.

k1p1-21.name: text#21
k1p1-21.text: Turn prediction–target mismatch into a score to minimize.

k1p2-2.name: text#2
k1p2-2.text: Subtract the target to obtain a residual

k1p2-4.name: text#4
k1p2-4.text: To measure how wrong, the first step is the gap between prediction and target.

k1p2-37.name: text#37
k1p2-37.text: Sign gives direction; the loss sets the penalty.

k1p3-4.name: text#4
k1p3-4.text: With residuals in hand, the first ruler: square, then add.

k1p3-19.name: text#19
k1p3-19.text: The squared-error sum is 103, before averaging.

k1p4-2.name: text#2
k1p4-2.text: Absolute error grows linearly with the miss

k1p4-4.name: text#4
k1p4-4.text: The second ruler: skip the square, just take absolute values.

k1p5-2.name: text#2
k1p5-2.text: Huber is quadratic nearby and linear farther away

k1p5-4.name: text#4
k1p5-4.text: Squared is harsh and absolute is lenient; Huber joins them.

k1p5-26.name: text#26
k1p5-26.text: Use a positive threshold; this example uses one.

k1p6-2.name: text#2
k1p6-2.text: Huber assigns 9.5 to a residual of ten

k1p6-4.name: text#4
k1p6-4.text: Apply Huber's two pieces to the same residuals.

k1p6-32.name: text#32
k1p6-32.text: The four Huber losses sum to 11.

k1p7-2.name: text#2
k1p7-2.text: Sum and mean differ by the batch size

k1p7-4.name: text#4
k1p7-4.text: Each ruler gives a sum; first, sum versus mean.

k1p7-25.name: text#25
k1p7-25.text:
Align the convention before comparing:
all sums or all means, never mixed

k1p8-2.name: text#2
k1p8-2.text: Use shares to see how much the outlier dominates

k1p8-4.name: text#4
k1p8-4.text: Totals are not enough; check what share the outlier takes.

k1p8-22.name: text#22
k1p8-22.text: Here, squared error gives the largest outlier share.

k1p9-2.name: text#2
k1p9-2.text: Three rulers respond differently to large errors

k1p9-4.name: text#4
k1p9-4.text: Draw the three rulers on one axis to see how they react to big errors.

k1p9-25.name: text#25
k1p9-25.text:
Curves compare growth,
not values across rulers

k1p9-27.name: text#27
k1p9-27.text: Compare growth patterns, not unlike numerical scales.

k1p10-4.name: text#4
k1p10-4.text: Regression measures distance; classification measures the probability given to the right answer.

k1p10-23.name: text#23
k1p10-23.text: softmax for multi-class; sigmoid for binary

k1p10-25.name: text#25
k1p10-25.text: For a one-hot target, take the true class’s negative log.

k1p11-2.name: text#2
k1p11-2.text: The same prediction has different losses for different targets

k1p11-4.name: text#4
k1p11-4.text: Use KP06's softmax output to compute cross-entropy for different right answers.

k1p11-28.name: text#28
k1p11-28.text: Use full-precision KP06 probabilities before rounding.

k1p12-4.name: text#4
k1p12-4.text: How is two-class cross-entropy written? Include both outcomes.

k1p12-22.name: text#22
k1p12-22.text: One probability and its complement, not a scalar summing to one.

k1p13-2.name: text#2
k1p13-2.text: KL compares target and predicted distributions

k1p13-4.name: text#4
k1p13-4.text: When the target is itself a distribution, use KL divergence.

k1p13-32.name: text#32
k1p13-32.text:
Direction matters:
it is measured from the target $\mathbf y$

k1p13-34.name: text#34
k1p13-34.text: Direction matters; predictions need support where targets do.

k1p14-2.name: text#2
k1p14-2.text: Compute every KL term before adding

k1p14-4.name: text#4
k1p14-4.text: Compute KL term by term with numbers.

k1p14-26.name: text#26
k1p14-26.text: single terms may be negative (red); only the total KL is never below 0

k1p14-28.name: text#28
k1p14-28.text: Individual terms may be negative; the total KL is nonnegative.

k1p15-2.name: text#2
k1p15-2.text: For fixed targets, cross-entropy and KL differ by a constant

k1p15-4.name: text#4
k1p15-4.text: How are cross-entropy and KL related?

k1p15-6.name: text#6
k1p15-6.text: $H(\mathbf y,\mathbf p)=H(\mathbf y)+D_{\rm KL}(\mathbf y\Vert\mathbf p)$

k1p15-21.name: text#21
k1p15-21.text: One-hot targets have zero entropy, so the two losses agree.

k1p16-2.name: text#2
k1p16-2.text: Hinge asks for a score margin, beyond a correct sign

k1p16-4.name: text#4
k1p16-4.text: A third classification ruler: hinge, which punishes even right-but-too-close.

k1p16-33.name: text#33
k1p16-33.text:
Yellow band: right side
but still within $m$, punished

k1p16-35.name: text#35
k1p16-35.text: Zero loss requires the signed score to reach the margin.

k1p17-2.name: text#2
k1p17-2.text: Three scores: safe, too close, and wrong

k1p17-17.name: text#17
k1p17-17.text: safe: right and beyond the margin

k1p17-36.name: text#36
k1p17-36.text: The second point is right ($0.3>0$) yet punished by $0.7$: it is within $m$

k1p17-38.name: text#38
k1p17-38.text: Compute the signed score before applying Hinge.

k1p18-2.name: text#2
k1p18-2.text: A score margin is not a geometric distance

k1p18-4.name: text#4
k1p18-4.text: Is hinge's margin really a distance?

k1p18-32.name: text#32
k1p18-32.text: Scaling weights and bias keeps the boundary but changes scores.

k1p19-2.name: text#2
k1p19-2.text: Huber joins values and slopes at both thresholds

k1p19-4.name: text#4
k1p19-4.text: (Optional) Back to Huber: do the two pieces join smoothly?

k1p19-25.name: text#25
k1p19-25.text:
values match and first derivatives match;
the second derivative still switches

k1p19-27.name: text#27
k1p19-27.text: The first derivative is continuous; the second changes.

k1p20-2.name: text#2
k1p20-2.text: Choose a loss after identifying the task

k1p20-4.name: text#4
k1p20-4.text: All six losses seen; gather them into one choosing table.

k1p20-11.name: text#11
k1p20-11.text: MSE smooth but amplifies outliers; MAE robust but not differentiable at 0; Huber in between, tune $\delta$

k1p20-15.name: text#15
k1p20-15.text: outputs must look like probabilities: in $[0,1]$, sum 1

k1p20-23.name: text#23
k1p20-23.text: e.g. distillation; differs from cross-entropy by a constant for a fixed target

k1p20-29.name: text#29
k1p20-29.text:
Like archery: loss is the arrow's distance from the bullseye;
classification measures probability against the answer

k1p20-31.name: text#31
k1p20-31.text: Real targets, classes, soft distributions and margins need different rulers.

k1p21-2.name: text#2
k1p21-2.text: Read a low loss with its data and ruler

k1p21-7.name: text#7
k1p21-7.text: “The smaller the loss, the better the network.”

k1p21-12.name: text#12
k1p21-12.text: No: the loss is measured on the training data only; a very small loss may just mean the data was memorized (KP04's generalization problem)

k1p21-16.name: text#16
k1p21-16.text: “Values of different losses can be compared directly.”

k1p21-21.name: text#21
k1p21-21.text: No: MSE's $103$ and MAE's $13$ say nothing about which is larger; they are different rulers

k1p21-24.name: text#24
k1p21-24.text: Low training loss does not ensure generalization; unlike losses are not comparable.

k1p22-2.name: text#2
k1p22-2.text: Next: learn a linear unit through squared error

k1p22-4.name: text#4
k1p22-4.text: We have a loss; next, how to make it smaller?

k1p22-10.name: text#10
k1p22-10.text: discrete: it jumps, with no slope to follow

k1p22-18.name: text#18
k1p22-18.text: continuous: a slope to walk down, step by step

k1p22-20.name: text#20
k1p22-20.text:
The Perceptron only counts mistakes and cannot learn by gradient;
switch to the continuous squared error and we can walk downhill: ADALINE (KP08)

k1p22-22.name: text#22
k1p22-22.text: KP08: ADALINE connects continuous error to weight updates.
